body: Similiar issue: If you delete an required input field from the form in the webapp and submit the form (actionUpdate), the model will be updated (with keeping the old value of the deleted field).
@cbhp either the validation is broken on update, or there is some misunderstanding of how the validation should work on update. Related issue: https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/issues/9134

https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/db/BaseActiveRecord.php#L213
says:
To use Optimistic locking:
[...]
2. Add a `required` validation rule for the version column to ensure the version value is submitted.

That is what I have done, with no effect.
@cbhp those docs are misleading, it turns out the rules are not for input validation, but for model validation, see https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/issues/9134

@EvgenyOrekhov I found the same issue for actionDelete.
If the POST-Request for deletion contains the 'version'-attribute, it will be checked. If not, you can delete the model..
Makes sense. Do you like to create a pull request?
Ok. I'll check it again to see if I find a better fix to source code. If not and no body else does I'll do a PR to update docs to recommend using virtual attribute as shown above.

issue.title: Optimistic lock problem
issue.body:
Optimistic lock logic is not taken into account when soft delete/restore

my quick fix
replace in delete/restore internal methods
```php
$result = $this->owner->updateAttributes($attributes);
```
with
```php
$this->owner->setAttributes($attributes, false);
$result = $this->owner->update(false, array_keys($attributes));
```
